quest.title: Night-Wind Letter
quest.description: You receive a letter from the Masters of the Night-Wind asking for your help, signed by Ororon. Just what could have happened...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Incense Ashcrystals x80, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Clairvoyance Model: Spiritloom x1, Clairvoyance Model: Projection Censer x1

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Once {NICKNAME} shows up, everything will get better...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Ororon, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Oh, hey there, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you were looking for us? We came as soon as we heard.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You did? That makes me feel... warm and fuzzy. Is this what happiness feels like?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...The heck? Where is this coming from...?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You are truly the best friends I could ask for. If my vegetables met you, I'm sure they'd grow all the more lush for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... what makes you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well, it's a compliment. I heard that complimenting people makes them happy. Did it work? Are you happy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very much so, but what about you? You don't look too happy.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's that obvious, huh? Well, you're right. I feel like an aphid who can't find a flower. Granny is standing in my way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yes. Granny's a genius, as you know. Geniuses often stand in the way of others, leading them to despair.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And on top of that, I'm her grandson. Which means I get a double dose of despair.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: If that sounds serious... it's because it is. So please, help me deal with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened, exactly? You make it sound so dramatic...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I had to get you involved. Most people can't deal with Granny, and...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #Exactly! You were the first person I thought of, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #{M#"Gramps"}{F#"Granny"} is what I called you when we first met, and I know I got told off for it... but please let me off for calling you that one more time.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: It feels like there's something unique about you. Even Granny Citlali treats you like you're someone special. And everything that's happened since we met suggests it's true.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: If I had a woven scroll that listed the forty people who can deal with Granny Citlali, your name would be at the top of that list.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so who are these other thirty-nine?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #They're also {NICKNAME}. A whole thirty-nine {NICKNAME} after the first one.

choices.text: You flatter me, but I'm too young to be a grandparent.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Please, you've gotta help me. This is really important.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Although it looks like I'm just hanging around with nothing to do, inside, I'm distraught about the path ahead. Granny Citlali is blocking my way and I can't get past.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: But now that you're here, I can start moving again. Before time runs out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, so what do you need me to do?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: You know how much Granny loves to drink, nap, and read light novels, right? If you offer her what she wants, I'm sure you can lure her away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean, use those things as bait to distract her, so she won't notice what you're up to?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: That's right. Don't worry, I won't make you do all the work — I've planned it all out, including what you need to say. All you need to do is walk up to her, and tell her this:

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: "Dear Granny, I have the latest volume of 'Mirage Warriors' here, along with a special-edition spinoff of 'The Case Files of Miss Orith.' Wanna read them together?"

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: She'll pretend not to be interested for a few seconds, then think of an excuse to say yes. As long as you're the one doing the fishing, she'll definitely take the bait.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You really think I have that effect on her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's just trying to butter you up! Even Paimon can tell. He's just saying whatever it takes to persuade you.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #No, I mean it. Granny might not say it out loud, but I can tell — she has a soft spot for {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you say so... Paimon's still not convinced, but if all we have to do is say a few words to Citlali, it's hardly putting us out.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: It'll be as easy as watering vegetables — and if my vegetables were here, they'd... Uh, sorry, there's no time for vegetable talk.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Just trust me. Let me take you to her. With you there, everything will be better.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #Great, so you're gonna help me, right {M#"Gramps"}{F#"Granny"}? I can't stress how important this is.

choices.text: Haha, and you think I can!?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: #Of course you can! You were the first person I thought of, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}.

talks.objective: Head to the location pointed out by Ororon

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's Granny... She's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: She was standing there at the cave entrance to stop me from going in. Standing right in my way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you meant literally standing in your way... This whole time, Paimon thought you were being metaphorical.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Granny says it's tacky when light novels use contrived metaphors. I don't wanna be tacky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but aren't you comparing yourself to a light novel? Isn't that kinda contrived...?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What? Oh... darn it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, looks like your path ahead has been cleared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Citlali probably figured there was no point standing in your way anymore. Ororon, whatever it is you so desperately need to do, you're now free to do it.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I don't think it'll be that simple... Granny wouldn't release me from her grasp so easily.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: She might have laid a trap for me. Or maybe when I get inside, I'll get caught by one of her surveillance spells...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But why would she want to stop you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let alone lay a trap for you! Unless... You haven't been up to no good again, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I just want to rescue someone... and Granny won't let me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rescue someone!? Oh no, what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Could I ask you to go inside and take a look at him? I think he should be safe for now, but he'll be at greater and greater risk as time goes by.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But then... What are you going to do?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'll have to wait outside, or I might fall into one of Granny's traps.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...You mean, you want us to fall into her traps instead?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #No, you'll be fine. Granny's traps will recognize it's {NICKNAME}, so they'll leave you alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Really? That's a thing?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Sure it is — I mean, I've told my aphids all about your heroic deeds, so I assume Granny's told her traps, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You can't just assume that!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Either way... I'm counting on you, {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, sounds like someone's life is at stake so we should probably head in and check things out.

talks.objective: Enter the cave to check on the situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! The woven scroll is ready! This looks like a person... Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's Sanhaj Kompore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean, THAT Sanhaj? Ororon's ancient name hero guy?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's right. He was not only one of the six heroes, but also a legendary Border Master of our tribe. Five hundred years on, and the remains of his spirit is still so strong...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: "Border Master" is a honorable title, by the way. It's only given to powerful figures, like Granny Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, not like me. The most powerful Border Masters can expand the borders of the Night Kingdom, and temporarily manifest part of it in the real world.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm no amateur with border spells, but Sanhaj is in a league of his own.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: They say his border mastery was what turned the tide in the Battle of the Mare Jivari five hundred years ago. Legend has it that Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom and exploded it to defeat the encroaching dark calamity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! He must have been really strong!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course, it came at a great price. As far as I understand, both Sanhaj and Tenoch, the leader of the tribal coalition forces, gave their lives to activate this spell.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I don't know what Leyla was thinking... Even I'd think twice before seeking out Sanhaj Kompore during clairvoyance, so what sort of spirit-duffer in their right mind would... Hmph, I guess folly is the greater part of bravery.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm starting to feel like something else is at play here. I think I'll pay a visit to his house and see if I can find any clues.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the other approach? Shall we keep that up while you're gone?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yep, you can keep gathering the roaming spirits, that won't be affected. Hopefully you do find Leyla that way, because it'll save us an awful lot of trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But before that, it looks like we now have another problem on our hands. Connecting with the spirit of Sanhaj Kompore has caused quite a stir... I think we may have just spooked all the monsters in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, if you've got some time, could you go and get them to pipe down a bit? We don't want them to start attacking innocent bystanders.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's fine, I can handle that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Oh no — you're staying right here, mister! {NICKNAME} has enough to do already without coming to your rescue.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Alright then... Sorry, {NICKNAME}. Over to you, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No problem, it'll be a piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't sweat it. The most important thing right now is getting Leyla's spirit back.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm heading out. See you guys later.

talks.objective: Enter the cave to check on the situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we made it in without a hitch! Maybe Citlali's traps can recognize us after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, look! There's someone there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi! Are you okay? Can you hear us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's not responding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is he asleep? Or sick? ...Do you think this is the guy Ororon was talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, what the heck's been going on here? Lots of strange and mysterious stuff around...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like some kind of ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, could be... Let's get Ororon in here. He'll know what this is all about.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Sorry, Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All grown up now, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...I'm truly sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now that you're one of the six heroes, you think you can do as you please, do you? Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well? Explain yourself, you dummy! How exactly were you thinking of helping that spirit-duffer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ororon! And, uhh... hey, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? HUH??? When did you guys...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #(Drat, I wasn't expecting them. And now {NICKNAME} probably caught me yelling at Ororon... Aah, this is not a good look for me!)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Haha... Hello there, you two. We were just, um... Ororon and I, we were, uh... play acting...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You know, acting out some scenes from a light novel, quoting the lines... I didn't actually mean what I was saying. Right, Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh... Yes, that's right.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #I owe you an apology too, {NICKNAME}. I asked you for help, but I forgot to watch my back, and Granny caught me... And now we're play-acting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what are you two up to, exactly? Did something happen to this poor guy?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yeah — Leyla's his name. He got into some trouble during a clairvoyance session.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Clairvoyance?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's a kind of spell that lets your spirit leave your body, so you can access secret knowledge. You know what a medium is, right? You've probably come across them in novels. Anyway, it's similar to that.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Leyla's problem is, his spirit has gotten lost and can't find its way back to his body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, in other words, his body's here, but his soul's gone!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Well, technically the soul and the spirit aren't quite the same thing... but yes, in a nutshell, that's basically it.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I just wanted to help bring Leyla's spirit back...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph, and I wouldn't have stopped him if it was anyone else. But the issue is, Mr. Leyla here is what we call a "spirit-duffer."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's a spirit-duffer?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Someone with no spiritual sensitivity whatsoever. Spirit-duffers can't sense or control spirits, much less use spells on them.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Now, there are certain methods that can force even spirit-duffers into a clairvoyant state, but... well, I mean, look what happened to Mr. Leyla.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The spells of the Masters of the Night-Wind are all based on dealing with spirits, and so are all our problem-solving methods. So for spirit-duffers, even our healing methods don't work on them.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: So if they get into trouble trying to use a spell, there's basically nothing we can do.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Yes, there is. As long as the soul is involved, I should be able to help...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You hear that? No prizes for guessing what Ororon's bright idea was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Because of your special constitution, right? But isn't that kinda risky for you?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'll be fine — Granny's just worrying too much. I'm feeling fine now, so I should be able to do it safely. Besides, it's probably our only hope of bringing Leyla back.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Don't kid yourself. What happens if it's not as safe as you're hoping, hmm? We both know you'll risk it all to try and rescue him anyway. Honestly, you're such an idiot sometimes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... This is a tricky one. It's true that Ororon can be self-sacrificing to a fault, but it's also true that Citlali tends to worry too much...

choices.text: I'm with Citlali on this. Ororon is being an idiot.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Call me an idiot all you want — I know I can bring his spirit back. I just need your support.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey! That's enough, you little squirt. Since when does the grandkid call the shots? Granny obviously knows how to handle this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You do?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Wait, really? You actually know a way to save him?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yes! I mean, it's a crude solution... but that's beside the point! The point being, don't interfere when Granny's already got things under control!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #Anyway. {NICKNAME}, I was actually going to ask for your help on this. My plan will take quite a lot of work, and it's a little too much for one person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, great! Well, it's a good thing Ororon brought us here then!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure, how can I help?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I intend to use a two-pronged approach. The first is the crude method — basically, it's looking for a needle in a haystack.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: See the thing I've drawn around Leyla's body? That's a gateway to the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Once the gateway is activated, all roaming spirits in the area will be drawn to it. If we're lucky, we'll find the one that belongs to Leyla.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'll lend you some of my power like last time, so you can use my clairvoyance. It only works if you use this projection censer first though, so don't forget that step.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Don't worry, this time nothing can go wrong! You'll just feel like you're in the Night Kingdom, and you'll see a lot of roaming spirits around you. All you need to do is gather them up.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You can leave Ororon to sift through them and find Leyla. Since he wants to help so bad, he can take the hardest job.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's the other approach?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Draw him back, using what I know about the instincts of spirits. As we all know, clairvoyance is usually conducted with the goal of unraveling mysteries.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: If we can find out what mystery Leyla wanted to learn the truth of, we can use that to draw his lost spirit back here.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'll do some clairvoyance of my own, and channel it through Leyla's body. That should give me some idea of what he was thinking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon thinks she gets it now. The first approach is like fishing with a net, and the second is like fishing with bait. Just like how Ororon wanted us to lure you away with the promise of light novels!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Um... Your point would have been just as clear without the example, Paimon.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What!? ...Don't think I won't revisit this later.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: But Granny, it's amazing that you can use a person as a clairvoyance medium. I always thought you had to use inanimate objects.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmph, you can't flatter your way out of this one! But you're not wrong. A person without a spirit is just a physical shell — which, for our purposes, makes them an inanimate object.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, just over there is my spiritloom, which will record the fragments I see during clairvoyance. Once I begin, please arrange them on a woven scroll for me.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Let me know when you're ready. We should get to work.

choices.text: I'm with Ororon. Citlali's the one being an idiot.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey! That's Granny Itztli to you! Who do you take me for? I obviously know how to handle this.

choices.text: I bet you've got a plan, huh, Citlali?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hehe, you're darn right Granny Itztli's got a plan! Why else do you think I'd be here?

choices.text: Just watch your back next time.
Play acting, huh? Can I join in?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on. Now's not the time for games.

talks.objective: Use the spiritloom to weave the scroll
Use the spiritloom to weave the scroll

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #You can do it, {NICKNAME}! Together, we'll bring Leyla back for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #You are the best, {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}. Please, can you go inside and take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Are you ready? Don't worry, the spiritloom is very easy to use.

choices.text: Alright, I'll give it a try.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I know this is your first time working with it, but I have a feeling you'll do great.

choices.text: I need a little more time.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we just keep following this path...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ororon seemed pretty confident that Citlali's traps won't harm us, but still, it can't hurt to be careful.
